day_shape: 82 items in a wartime frame: CENTCOM says its Iran blockade has redirected 49 vessels and Trump says a Hormuz deal is near, IDF strikes across southern Lebanon after two reservists killed at Majdal Zoun, Houthi attacks kill 30+ Yemeni troops and hit Saudi Arabia, and Iranian outlets amplify reports of US munitions shortages; nothing from UK Parliament, IAEA or OFAC.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz blockade and Iran standoff
threads.summary: Trump told reporters he expects a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz soon, while CENTCOM said US forces have redirected 49 commercial vessels, disabled two and boarded two as of Aug 6. Iran's Mohsen Rezaei said on regime channels that Tehran will not allow a 'second corridor' in the strait and warned US ships face serious losses if the blockade continues.

threads.label: US munitions shortages and war costs
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post and Times of Israel reported Trump was angered by disclosures of dwindling US munitions stockpiles that could constrain further action against Iran, with some interceptor stocks reportedly around 20% of Pentagon targets. Iranian state media amplified the reporting and cited a CSIS estimate that the war has cost the Pentagon $34–42 billion, including $18.5bn on Patriot and THAAD interceptors.

threads.label: Southern Lebanon strikes after IDF deaths
threads.summary: The IDF said it struck weapons depots, a command centre and other Hezbollah infrastructure across southern Lebanon in response to a booby-trap explosion at Majdal Zoun that killed two reservists — Maj. (res.) Harel Birenstock and Sgt. Maj. (res.) Tamir Vaknin — and wounded four. The IDF also said it had located thousands of Hezbollah facilities in southern villages, and a Jerusalem Post editorial and former Mossad official Oded Ailam called for intensified strikes short of ending the ceasefire.

threads.label: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemen
threads.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said two people were killed and 11 injured in Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Jerusalem Post reported at least 30 Yemeni government troops killed in Houthi missile and drone attacks on camps in Marib and Hadramout. Bloomberg-cited reporting and Iranian outlets said Riyadh is pursuing back-channel diplomacy with the Houthis, and Turkish media said Erdogan will meet MBS and Pakistan's PM in a trilateral on Friday.

threads.label: US oil imports and Saudi supply disruption
threads.summary: Bloomberg reported, and Iranian outlets amplified, that Saudi crude exports to the US fell to zero in July for the first time since 1985 as US refiners switched to Venezuelan and other suppliers. Defa Press and IRIB attributed the shift to tanker-route disruption from the US–Iran war in the Gulf.

threads.label: Iran domestic repression and January protests fallout
threads.summary: Iran International reported five January-protest detainees face execution in the Mashhad area, a second case has been opened against jailed protester Ahmad Seyyed-Abdollahi, and UN human rights experts said Iran has intensified repression of Kurdish and Baluch minorities. President Masoud Pezeshkian rejected higher death-toll estimates from the January crackdown and called those citing them 'traitors', drawing public backlash, while activists renewed calls for Freiburg to end its twinning with Isfahan after two public executions.

threads.label: Gaza operations and disarmament plan
threads.summary: Times of Israel reported IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir toured Gaza saying the army was 'systematically striking Hamas' as Israel pushes back on a US-backed disarmament plan requiring a halt to operations, and the Jerusalem Post reported Trump's Board of Peace issued its first Gaza construction contract. Israel's UN ambassador Danny Danon cited a UNICEF-led malnutrition survey to argue the 'false narrative against Israel' was collapsing.

events.title: Five January protest detainees face execution in northeast Iran

events.title: Italy says Lion and Sun flag removed from Tajani X post over technical issue

events.title: Executions in Isfahan renew calls to end German city partnership
events.summary: The public execution of two protesters in Isfahan has renewed calls for the German city of Freiburg to end its 25-year twinning with the Iranian city, with activists arguing the partnership lends legitimacy to a state punishing dissent with death penalty.

events.title: Iran women’s footballers who sought asylum become Australian citizens

events.title: Iran's energy crisis is political, not seasonal
events.summary: In Iran, the authorities call it a scheduled outage. The electricity will be disconnected for two hours. The water may return later in the evening. Families are instructed to adjust their lives to temporary emergencies. But there is no pause button for daily life.
